title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Providing a Second Opinion
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A person who is currently represented by another paralegal contacts you to ask for a second opinion on their ongoing WSIB claim. They feel their current paralegal is giving them bad advice. Can you provide this second opinion?
options: No, it is professional misconduct to communicate with a person who is already represented.
Yes, but you must first notify the original paralegal that you are reviewing the file.
Yes, a paralegal may provide a second opinion to a represented person without notifying the first paralegal.
No, unless the client formally fires the first paralegal in writing.
questions.explain: Under Rule 7.02 (Communication with a represented person), while a paralegal generally cannot communicate with an opposing party who is represented, the rule does not prevent a paralegal from providing a second opinion directly to a person who is seeking it, and they do not need to notify the incumbent representative.
